### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**18** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `96c93b7787545281da05a2579faaf2f6ec1c2d57` — the merge of head `f0519ad0f54cbb47b050e43c26f1860b8d00d6b3` into base `d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 96c93b7787545281da05a2579faaf2f6ec1c2d57 && git checkout 96c93b7787545281da05a2579faaf2f6ec1c2d57
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a f0519ad0f54cbb47b050e43c26f1860b8d00d6b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a && git merge --no-ff f0519ad0f54cbb47b050e43c26f1860b8d00d6b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f0519ad0f54cbb47b050e43c26f1860b8d00d6b3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-page-variables.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.page-variable-references.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/page-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/predicate-rhs-position.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/usePageVariables.tsx, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/usePageVariableActionBridge.tsx, ui/packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/record-picker.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/text-input.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/page-variables.page.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/contact-form.page.ts. Not reviewed (prose face): .changeset/28725-page-variable-source-and-read.md, read for ② only.

Check-runs on the head: 67 runs, 56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 cancelled, 0 pending (read with `--paginate`; a Check Changeset re-run that was in progress at the first read finished green). Green include Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint and the other Lint jobs, Type Check (workspace, source, consumer, debt ledger, UI), Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Page writes: a `variables[i].source` naming no component `id` the page holds is refused with `page-variable-source-unknown` at `variables[i].source`. RIGHT. The spec declares `source` as "Component id that writes this variable" (page.zod.ts line 913) and retired the reverse `targetVariable` keys on the two writers because the binding "is resolved from the page variable whose `source` names this component's `id`" (component.zod.ts lines 3271-3337); the console resolves it exactly so, `definitions.find` on `d.source === componentId` called with `schema.id` by `record-picker.tsx` and `text-input.tsx`, the only two callers. A `source` no component carries binds nothing, so the variable keeps its default for the page's life: a declared binding that never resolves, refused where it was written. Component ids come from `walkPageComponents`, the one shared walk whose slot positions derive from the spec's own list (regions, slots, every `properties` sub-tree including `page:tabs` / `page:accordion` panels), read once per page and only when some entry has a `source`; a `kind: 'react'` or `'html'` page yields nothing from that walk and is not judged, which is the right stand-down (its components live in the source). Case is compared exactly, as the console compares it.
2. Page writes: a page component `visibleWhen` reading `page.NAME` or `page.?NAME` for a `NAME` the page's `variables` does not declare is refused with `visibility-page-variable-undeclared` at the component, naming the first such read. RIGHT. The spec binds `page.VAR` to "page state" declared in `variables` (page.zod.ts lines 770, 884, 1964); the console's `buildNodeEvaluationScope` writes `page: pageVariables` after the ambient spread (SchemaRenderer.tsx lines 699-712), so nothing else can supply `page`; the store is seeded from the declarations alone, mounted only when the page declares variables (page.tsx line 973), and its writers are the two bound elements (declared names only) and a dashboard's filter bar, which mounts its own nested provider for its own declared filters (DashboardRenderer.tsx line 1583) and whose writes reach the page scope only for a name the page defines. No other `setVariable` caller exists in `ui/`. So an undeclared member of `page` is never present; the read faults and the element renders, the fail-open the family's other gating ids refuse. Judged from the AST the `has()` check already holds (no second parser), on page components only; a comprehension that binds `page` as its loop variable stands the predicate down, and an index read is not judged, both missed catches rather than false errors. A `has(page.nosuch)` or `page.?nosuch.orValue(...)` guard on an undeclared name is refused too, rightly: the name can never exist on that page, so the guard is dead code the author did not mean.
3. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`: `PAGE_VARIABLE_SOURCE_UNKNOWN` and `VISIBILITY_PAGE_VARIABLE_UNDECLARED` exported; two `os explain` entries (`covers` under 60 characters without a period, no issue number in a paragraph). No registry change: both ids live in rules already wired on `page` writes (`validatePageVariables`, `validateVisibilityPredicates`), so `rulesRun`, the CLI rule count and the `content/docs` transcripts do not move, and the nav walker is untouched by the two new verdicts. RIGHT.
4. One implementation at every surface: save door, draft `_diagnostics` and publish through `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` over the same registry, the CLI through `runAuthoringRules('validate')`; the protocol tests pin the draft read (`variables.0.source`, `regions.0.components.0`), the 422 and the active save with the build's message; the lint tests pin door and `os validate` parity. RIGHT.
5. The fold: `checkElement`'s bounds arm and `navOverBudgetFinding` are replaced by one `overBudgetFinding(refusal, where, path, surface, root)` with `SyntaxSurface.overBudgetHint(root)`; `navOverBudgetFinding` is removed. Wording byte-identical on the tree, judged by reading both sides against `origin/main`: the message is the same template (`overruns ${boundName(...)}`, the summary echoed only when the bound is unnamed, then the surface's consequence, which is `NEVER_EVALUATES` for `ELEMENT_SURFACE` and the nav clause for `NAV_SURFACE`); the element hint string with `${root}.f in ['a', 'b', …]` and the formula/rollup clause is character-for-character the old arm's with the same `CANONICAL_ROOT_BY_LAYER[layer]` root; the nav hint is the 130-character #28756 line unchanged. The existing pins (the page/view over-budget cases in `validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts`, the #28726 nav block with its 200-character line pin) are untouched and green. RIGHT; the nav call passes an unused `'record'` root, commented as such.
6. Fixture triage: two clean controls that read `page.selectedId` / `page.selectedProjectId` on pages declaring no variables now declare them, and the page door family set gains the new id so the controls also assert its silence. RIGHT: a declaration added, not a predicate respelled.
7. Corpus: the shipped pages carry 3 `source` bindings and 5 `page.NAME` predicate reads, all on the two showcase pages and all resolving (read in `page-variables.page.ts` and `contact-form.page.ts`); the `source:` keys on the other showcase pages are page data bindings, not variables. 0 refused. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28725-page-variable-source-and-read.md`: `@objectstack/lint` **minor**, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason (the skills name `page.VAR` in root tables and teach no `source` binding), one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the no-conversion argument and the corpus count. Matches what the diff publishes: two references an author could write are now refused at every door (narrowed), on the one package the diff moves; `metadata-protocol` changes are tests only. The `(narrowing)` arm is the BREAKING one by AGENTS.md and the kind takes at least minor; the fold publishes nothing new. The PR body carries the same lines; Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is right; the claim comment's bare `no` is the seat's own line (③ item 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

Deviations, each answered:
1. Claim line `Clause-②: no` versus PR body and changeset `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Answered: the PR body and changeset are the records the gates read and they are right; the seat amends its claim comment; no PR change.
2. Two `metadata-protocol` test files added (test only) beyond the claim's `packages/lint/src` surface. Answered: #28723's and #28756's precedent and the only proof of the three doors; no source edit there.
3. The seat-ordered fold reported as not done in the os-dev-report, then done in the PR body's patch round. Answered on the tree: head `f0519ad0` carries the fold (① item 5); the report predates the commit.
4. `check:type-check-debt` first read a lock queue-timeout; re-run exit 0. Answered: Type Check · debt ledger is green on the head.
5. Dogfood battery not re-measured at `f0519ad0` (lint-only byte-identical refactor plus a merge). Answered: Dogfood Regression Gate is green on the head.

Out-of-scope observations the dev reported, each a missed catch and escalated for the seat's filing judgment, not this PR:
6. `page.NAME` reads outside a component `visibleWhen` are not resolved: props-bag CEL slots (`page:tabs` item predicates, which bind a different evaluator anyway) and `{{page.NAME}}` interpolation tokens in action bodies (`bodyExtra`, action.zod.ts line 1799). Agreed as outside the card's two observed shapes.
7. A `source` naming a component that exists but cannot write (only `element:record_picker` and `element:text_input` bind) still binds nothing. Agreed: the card and ruling ask for existence; a writer-capability check would be a new rule over the component vocabulary.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the consumer: the spec says `source` names the writer component's `id` and `page.VAR` is the page's declared state; the console binds both exactly that way and nowhere else. A `source` with no matching id and a `page.NAME` with no declaration are references the spec declares as resolvable only against the page itself and that never resolve there, so refusing them at the author makes the spec's own contract real and takes no working capability away. Attempts to break it: a writer nested in a container, a tabs panel or a slot is found by the shared walk (pinned for `properties.children`); a source-authored page is not judged on `source`; the console mounts no provider for a page without variables and no outer provider exists in the shell, so a variable-less page reading `page.X` really has nothing to read (there is no component that embeds one page inside another's scope; the dashboard's nested scope is the dashboard's own and a page component outside it cannot read its filters without declaring the name, which is exactly what the rule asks); `has()`-guarded declared reads, deeper reads through a declared `object` variable, variables with no `source`, and comprehension-bound `page` are all admitted; two undeclared reads are one finding; the differential at the door stays clean because `pages` is not a context collection. Hint lines are 172 and 117 characters. The fold is byte-identical by construction, with one builder per id as `syntaxFinding` already does.

Findings:
- Must-fix: none.
- Should-fix: none. The two observations in ③ items 6 and 7 are the seat's to file or decline; neither is a defect of this change.
